claim: The shape of an out-of-focus highlight is most of a night film's identity - a stadium behind a shallow lens is nothing but bokeh. Hexagonal reads mechanical and period, oval_anamorphic reads expensive, swirly reads unstable and antique.
method: identical subject sentence and seed in every panel; only the option clause changes. panels marked control render the untouched subject, because SDXL cannot express absence.

panels.clause: oval bokeh, anamorphic bokeh, stretched highlights
cat's eye bokeh, clipped highlights at frame edges
bloom, glowing orbs, soft light blobs

review.issue: Aperture-blade shape is not in the danbooru vocabulary. Animagine has one "bokeh" concept, so hexagonal, oval_anamorphic and cats_eye will most likely all render as ordinary round highlights — six options for roughly three looks (generic bokeh / swirly / bloom). Compounding it, the fixed subject sentence contains no shallow-DOF cue, so any panel whose clause does not itself say "blurry background" may have no bokeh at all to shape. bloom_blobs also duplicates lens.flare.warm_bloom and fx.glow.
review.fix: Put an identical DOF anchor in every clause ("blurry background, bokeh" in all six — constant across panels, so the method still holds), and cut the card to the shapes the model can draw: circular, swirly, oval_anamorphic, plus bloom_blobs only if flare.warm_bloom is dropped.
